summary: At the current B15 evaluation, the only remaining stop is applying the newly wished, uncursed unicorn horn while the Wizard is still blinded by the earlier cursed potion. C enters apply.c:use_unicorn_horn(), collects timed blindness as the only trouble, draws the uncursed cure limit, calls make_blinded(u.ucreamed, TRUE), and prints 'You can see again.' JavaScript's doapply() has no UNICORN_HORN case and stops in its unsupported default. The prior peffect_blindness stop is resolved and belongs only to the stale 26-screen record.

source.branch: In use_unicorn_horn(), obj is present and uncursed, so C skips the cursed adverse-effect branch. HBlinded has a timeout greater than u.ucreamed, the hero is not swallowed by an engulfer whose attack sustains blindness, and no other timed trouble qualifies. trouble_count is therefore one (BLINDED); no trouble shuffle is needed. With this unblessed horn, C evaluates rn2(d(2,2)), gets d(2,2)=3 and rn2(3)=2, clamps val_limit to one, and calls make_blinded(u.ucreamed, TRUE). In this recording u.ucreamed is zero, so the timed blindness is cleared and C displays 'You can see again.'
callers: apply.c:doapply() dispatches UNICORN_HORN to use_unicorn_horn(&obj) at lines 4370–4371; the void call leaves doapply()’s initial ECMD_TIME result intact.
The runtime input path is the apply command, inventory selection of the wished horn, then js/apply.js:doapply(); its switch omits UNICORN_HORN and the default throws for object type 261.
dependencies: The reached BLINDED cure delegates to potion.c:make_blinded(), already implemented in js/potion.js; preserve the HBlinded timeout, u.ucreamed threshold, swallowed-engulfer immunity, and feedback ordering.
The full C function also needs the multiple-trouble shuffle (shuffle_int_array(), when trouble_count > 1); no JavaScript implementation was found in the targeted source search.

Other use_unicorn_horn() branches call make_sick(), make_vomiting(), and make_stunned(), which remain explicit unported gaps in js/timeout.js; make_blinded(), make_confused(), make_hallucinated(), make_deaf(), and vomit() have JavaScript implementations. These branches are outside this case’s uncursed single-blindness path but remain part of a whole-function port.
